newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Meekatharra gets Indonesia mine OK.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Meekatharra gets Indonesia mine OK.

text.p: Australian miner Meekatharra Minerals Ltd said on Wednesday that final environmental approval had been granted by the Indonesian government for development of the Way Lingo gold and silver mine in Sumatra.
Gold production is scheduled to start later this year following completion of construction work and financing.
Way Lingo has a current resource of 187,000 ounces of gold equivalent and is expected to produce 30,000 ounces of gold and 500,000 ounces of silver annually, the company said.
Meekatharra holds an 85 percent interest in the project.
The remainder is owned by the Indonesian government.

Meekatharra last week placed with domestic and international investors 5.78 million shares to raise A$2.77 million. Canadian resources group Teck Corp has subscribed A$500,000 of the issue, representing 1.04 million shares, Meekatharra said.
The subscription is one of several ties between the two companies, including the Muarawahau gold project near the giant Busang gold find, potentially one of the world's largest.
"The purpose of the fundraising is for advancing gold exploration in Indonesia and general working capital," Meekatharra general manager Neil Arthur told Reuters.
Muarawahau is located about 50 km along the strike zone of Busang inside the "Trans-Borneo gold belt," which also hosts the Mount Muro and Kelian mines.
Evaluation of options for a North American stock exchange listing of Meekatharra's Indonesian properties were at an advanced stage, Arthur said.
Meekatharra holds a 45 percent interest in the Muarawahau project. It also is conducting exploration of several additional properties in Indonesia.
